A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Foresight Diffusion study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and matchable despite retitling, renumbering, and additional experiments in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original robot video prediction experiments on RoboNet and RT-1, scientific forecasting experiments on HeterNS, and architectural ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds guidance, training-control, predictor-quality, and calibration experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds an evaluated ForeDiff inference variant using classifier-free guidance (Section 4.1, Table 2). The default architecture, predictive and denoising objectives, frozen predictive representations, and two-stage training remain unchanged. The new joint-training and training-only variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same RoboNet action-conditioned prediction, RT-1 instruction-conditioned prediction, and HeterNS forecasting tasks. The additional studies retain these datasets and input scenarios; no new domain, population, or task coverage is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds CFG-guided vanilla diffusion, a training-only decoupling comparator, and joint-loss training variants (Tables 2, 10, and 11). The original comparison methods, including MaskViT, SVG, GHVAE, FitVid, and iVideoGPT, remain in the corresponding benchmark comparison.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation design with CFG inference, pretraining at t=1 followed by full-timestep fine-tuning, joint-loss weights of 0.1 and 1, and earlier predictor checkpoints. It adds CRPS, NLL, and coverage evaluation, while Figure 3c replaces LPIPS with latent MSE. Existing benchmark resolutions, prediction horizons, and default training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained PredHead, block-count, and parameter-scaling ablations, v2 tests whether training decoupling alone suffices, whether joint training can replace two-stage training, and sensitivity to predictor quality (Tables 10–12). CFG compatibility and calibration analyses additionally examine alternative explanations for improved consistency.

E5.justification: v2 introduces predictive-uncertainty calibration reporting through empirical-versus-nominal coverage curves and CRPS/NLL evaluation. The existing per-condition STD calculation over typically 100 generated samples is unchanged. Neither version reports uncertainty across independent training runs, confidence intervals for benchmark estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original tabulated benchmark and ablation scores are retained, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 2 and 10–13. For example, ForeDiff with CFG reports LPIPS 5.05 and STDLPIPS 0.24, versus 5.25 and 0.35 without CFG. Calibration results favor ForeDiff on CRPS/NLL, while Figure 9 shows vanilla diffusion closer to ideal coverage. Figure 3c also adds latent-MSE results.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1 and Appendix A retain the same reparameterization, bias-variance argument, and deterministic-model reduction. Replacing T with t=1 and clarifying the final network argument are notational and explanatory edits. Streamlining the preliminary forward-process equations introduces no substantive theoretical change.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that conditioning–denoising entanglement limits predictive ability and that architectural separation with predictor pretraining improves accuracy and consistency. Replacing 'world modeling' with 'predictive learning' does not change the formal prediction problem or the principal contributions; the added experiments support retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning CFG complementarity, the necessity of architectural and training decoupling, tolerance of imperfect predictors, possible predictor overfitting, and calibration versus mode collapse. It attributes vanilla diffusion's better coverage to inflated uncertainty. Appendix E replaces the pretrained-predictor and open-loop limitations with lack of large-scale validation and restriction to DiT backbones, retaining the diffusion-family boundary.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds concrete instructions for the new controls: t=1 pretraining followed by uniformly weighted timestep fine-tuning, the composite loss and its weights, and 0.5M/0.8M predictor checkpoints. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, and dataset-processing disclosures remain unchanged. Guidance strength and calibration-estimation details are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a sampling-methods discussion positioning ForeDiff as complementary to guidance, noise manipulation, and inference-time scaling, with new references to Ho and Salimans, Ahn, Zhou, and Ma. Planning/control references to Ebert and Hirose disappear. Most prior diffusion and non-diffusion positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, author information, and terminology throughout, edits the introduction and method explanations, streamlines the preliminaries, and revises related work and limitations. It also adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain largely intact, and much existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially extends the visual presentation with CFG, training-control, checkpoint, and calibration tables plus coverage plots. It redraws the introductory task diagram, swaps and relocates the original Figures 1–2, revises Figure 3c's metrics and axes, and adopts an ICLR layout. Most existing benchmark visualizations remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: The added training-only, joint-loss, and checkpoint controls strengthen the evidence for ForeDiff's existing design, while CFG and calibration evaluations address useful alternative explanations. These gains are limited by missing guidance/calibration implementation details and a stronger calibration interpretation despite coverage favoring vanilla diffusion. Removing the explicit open-loop limitation also loses a useful qualification. Overall, the additional scrutiny provides a modest net improvement.
